scope:
Add `shiki contract amend --target <path> --plan <amended plan>` to `scripts/shiki_cli.py` and `scripts/shiki_tasks.py`, modelled on the existing `cmd_contract_open`. Given an amended spec-frozen plan for a goal already registered on the default branch, it rewrites the goal's registered task files to the amended plan's definitions, sets the affected tasks' `status` to `ready`, restores the DAG, and appends a `contract-amended` ledger entry. It prints the marker, the goal id and the required PR body sections, and it prints the SAME `maintainer_action_required` refusal `cmd_contract_open` prints — it must NOT apply the `mergegate:amendment` label, because the label is the independent second factor and self-applying it would collapse two factors to one.

The command must refuse, with a precise message, when: the goal is not registered on the default branch; the plan is not the goal's `source_plan`; the plan is not spec-frozen; the plan's `spec_freeze.amendments` does not extend the registered plan's by at least one entry; or a task title in the amended plan does not resolve to a registered task. It must not write anything on any refusal path.

Document `mergegate:amendment` in `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` alongside the existing `mergegate:` labels, stating that it is maintainer-applied and what it authorizes. Write `docs/adr/0018-contract-amendment-delivery.md` recording the decision: Context (the three measured blocks and why each is correct, and that PR #229 closed the last unguarded route on 2026-08-01), Decision (two-factor mode, append-only spec_freeze relaxation, plan-as-authority, risk never weaker than base, lifecycle fields constrained), Alternatives (reusing `mergegate:contract` and auto-detecting from a MODIFY, rejected because one operator act would mean two different things; keeping amendments out of PRs entirely, rejected because it loses branch protection and the audit trail), and Consequences.

Add `tests/test_contract_amend_cli.py` covering the happy path and every refusal above, asserting in each refusal case that no file was written. Add control-plane assertions that the CLI does not apply the label and that `triage-labels.md` documents `mergegate:amendment`.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: the amendment mode from the previous task is enforced and unusable, because assembling a conforming Amendment PR by hand means rewriting several task files to match an amended plan, restoring the DAG, and appending the right ledger type — every one of which the gate checks and none of which is scripted. The first hand-assembled attempt fails the gate on a detail, and each retry costs a full CI round.
  Precedent: `shiki contract open` exists for exactly this reason on the registration path, and prints a refusal rather than applying `mergegate:contract` itself. `shiki contract amend` is its counterpart and must refuse in the same way for the same reason.
  Exact change that reproduces this result: a CLI that renders the amendment from the amended plan, and a documented label so the operator knows what they are being asked to approve.
  Reproducible when: an operator amends a plan, runs one command, opens a PR, applies one label, and the gate passes on the first attempt.
